15	---
16	
17	When we stop a for-each, we continue to show the progress bar. this is ok, but the position is lost, we should keep this so we can find the last position easier again
18	
19	## Current state
20	
21	`ActionRun.executeAgentForEach` publishes `forEachProgress` before the first selected record and after each processed record. Cancellation does not count the interrupted record as processed, so the last published `processedCount` already identifies the next start index.
22	
23	`ActionRunRegistry` stores this progress while the run is active, but clears it for every terminal status, including `cancelled`. The popup progress indicator reads only this live run value. The conversation persists its for-each configuration, but not its progress, so the position is unavailable after cancellation, run-store release, or reopening the conversation.
24	
25	## Implementation details
26	
27	- Add optional `forEachProgress` to the canonical `AgentConversation` and validate `processedCount` and `totalCount` as safe non-negative integers with `processedCount <= totalCount`.
28	- When a for-each run is cancelled, persist its latest published progress on the active conversation before publishing the terminal run event. The persisted value must remain the count of completed records; the interrupted record is not completed.
29	- Preserve cancelled for-each progress in `ActionRunRegistry`. Continue clearing transient interaction state and clear progress for successful completion and other terminal outcomes.
30	- Update `ForEachProgressIndicator` to use live run progress first and the selected persisted conversation progress otherwise. Do not change the run-button behavior, which shows progress only while a run is active.
31	- Keep progress scoped to its conversation and run. Starting another run must not reuse progress from a previously cancelled run.
32	- Add focused tests for activity persistence and parsing, cancellation ordering, registry terminal handling, and live-to-historical popup rendering.
33	
34	## Acceptance criteria
35	
36	- Stopping a non-empty for-each run leaves the popup progress bar at the last completed-record count.
37	- A record interrupted by Stop is not counted as processed. The displayed `processedCount` is the zero-based start index to use when resuming with the first unprocessed record.
38	- The stopped position remains available after closing and reopening the conversation and after reloading the project.
39	- Progress that starts from a non-zero `startIndex` retains that initial offset after cancellation.
40	- Completed records and failed records handled by `logAndContinue` count as processed before a later cancellation.
41	- Successful completion and non-cancellation failure retain their current terminal behavior and do not leave historical for-each progress visible.
42	- Ordinary actions and empty for-each runs do not show a for-each progress bar.
43	- Progress from one conversation or run never appears on another conversation or run.

4	internalId: 644f4bf0-b21a-42ba-be1e-5b0daaecb1b8

14	worktree: 2
15	---
16	
17	a link for creating an email should open the systems default email program
18	
19	## Current state
20	
21	An email link is a Markdown link whose URL uses the `mailto:` protocol. Two MD² link surfaces can receive one, and both currently end without opening an email program.
22	
23	- Conversation messages: `react-markdown` keeps `mailto:` URLs, and `remark-gfm` turns bare email addresses into `mailto:` links. `ActionConversationLink` leaves these links to the browser engine, so a click starts a main-frame navigation (a navigation of the whole MD² window). `handleFrameNavigation` in `desktop/src/shell/renderer_security.js` cancels that navigation to protect the app, then opens nothing because `isApprovedExternalUrl` accepts only `http:` and `https:`.
24	- Markdown editor: the link dialog Open action calls `openMarkdownLink`. `routeJsonLink` ignores URLs with a protocol, and `EXTERNAL_LINK_PROTOCOLS` then rejects `mailto:`, so `window.open` is never called.
25	
26	Approved web links already reach the system through `shell.openExternal`, which hands the URL to the operating system's default program for that protocol. `window.open` requests reach it through `handleWindowOpen`.
27	
28	## Implementation details
29	
30	- Add `mailto:` to `APPROVED_EXTERNAL_PROTOCOLS` in `desktop/src/shell/renderer_security.js`. Both `isApprovedExternalUrl` call sites, `handleFrameNavigation` and `handleWindowOpen`, need the new behavior.
31	- Add `mailto:` to `EXTERNAL_LINK_PROTOCOLS` in `app/src/components/editor/links/markdown_link_dialog_navigation.ts`. The Open action then uses the existing `window.open` path, and `handleWindowOpen` passes the URL to `shell.openExternal`.
32	- Do not change `ActionConversationLink`. A `mailto:` click stays a main-frame navigation attempt, and the guard cancels it before opening the email program, so MD² stays on the current view.
33	- Pass the URL unchanged, so `to`, `subject`, and `body` values reach the email program. Do not add parsing, validation, or other protocols.
34	- Do not add new failure UI. If `shell.openExternal` rejects, for example because the system cannot open the link, the rejection continues to the existing main-process `unhandledRejection` telemetry.
35	- Browser sessions served by the remote-control server need no separate code. The browser applies its own `mailto:` handling on the device showing MD².
36	- Tests:

## Change plan for F_469 (`mailto:` links)

I checked the code, and the spec's description of the current state is accurate. Both allowlists (lists of link protocols MD² will hand to the operating system) currently contain only `http:` and `https:`. No edits have been made yet.

**Block 1: Desktop guard (`desktop/src/shell/renderer_security.js`)**
- Add `'mailto:'` to `APPROVED_EXTERNAL_PROTOCOLS`.
- Both callers get the new behaviour. When a conversation link is clicked, the window tries to navigate to it. `handleFrameNavigation` cancels that navigation and then calls `shell.openExternal`, which opens the default email program. `handleWindowOpen` does the same for `window.open` requests.
- Tests in `renderer_security.test.mjs`:
  - Move `mailto:user@example.com` out of the "blocks untrusted main-frame navigation" cases and into the "blocks navigation and opens externally" cases.
  - Add a new-window case for `mailto:` with expected result "opens externally".

**Block 2: Editor link dialog (`app/src/components/editor/links/markdown_link_dialog_navigation.ts`)**
- Add `'mailto:'` to `EXTERNAL_LINK_PROTOCOLS`. The Open action then calls `window.open`, which goes through `handleWindowOpen` to `shell.openExternal`.
- Test: add `mailto:user@example.com?subject=Hi&body=Text` to the opened URLs in `markdown_link_dialog_navigation.test.ts`. This checks that the URL is passed through unchanged.

**Block 3: Conversation link (test only)**
- No change to `ActionConversationLink`, as the spec requires. `isExternalWebLink` only matches `http(s)`, so a `mailto:` link gets no `_blank` target and opens through Block 1.
- Test in `action_conversation_message.test.tsx`: render `[mail](mailto:user@example.com)` and a bare `user@example.com`. Assert both have href `mailto:user@example.com` and no `target="_blank"`.

**Block 4: Verify and close out**
- Run the three test files and lint in `app` and `desktop`.
- Set `status: ready` in the feature description file in the `md2` repo.

**Edge cases**
- `file:`, `javascript:`, `about:` and `md2:` stay blocked. The existing tests already cover this.
- If `shell.openExternal` fails, the rejection goes to the existing `unhandledRejection` telemetry. No new error UI is added.

I've created tasks 1–4 for these blocks. Shall I go ahead?

F_469 is implemented: `mailto:` links now go to the system's default email program. The related tests pass (16 in `app` across two files, 16 in `desktop`). I haven't tried it in the running desktop app, so no email program has actually opened yet.

**Code changes**
- `desktop/src/shell/renderer_security.js`: added `'mailto:'` to `APPROVED_EXTERNAL_PROTOCOLS`. Clicking an email link in a conversation tries to navigate the whole MD² window to it. That navigation is still cancelled, so MD² stays on the current view and unsaved editor content is kept, and the link now goes to `shell.openExternal`. `window.open` requests get the same treatment.
- `app/src/components/editor/links/markdown_link_dialog_navigation.ts`: added `'mailto:'` to `EXTERNAL_LINK_PROTOCOLS`. Open in the editor's link dialog now calls `window.open`, which ends up at `shell.openExternal`.
- The URL is passed through unchanged, so `subject` and `body` reach the email program.
- `ActionConversationLink` is unchanged.

**Tests**
- `renderer_security.test.mjs`:
  - Moved `mailto:` from the blocked navigation cases to the opened-externally cases, using a link with `subject` and `body`.
  - Added a new-window case for `mailto:`.
  - `file:`, `javascript:` and `md2:` stay blocked.
- `markdown_link_dialog_navigation.test.ts`: the Open action is now checked for a `mailto:` link with `subject` and `body`.
- `action_conversation_message.test.tsx`: new tests check that an explicit `mailto:` link and a bare email address both render with href `mailto:user@example.com` and without `target="_blank"`.

**Lint:** I ran ESLint only on the five files I changed, and it was clean. I didn't run the full `npm run lint`.

**Status:** I set `status: ready` in `C:\Users\janbo\Documents\dev\md2\design/feature_descriptions/F_469_add_support_to_email_links.md`.
